<!-- pr-reviewer: 1b4c37adddc5a5bedb7f2e630fe39727c90fceca -->

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** I found no code blockers. The label is `needs-maintainer`: this PR adds a new local protocol (the UI link), and the Windows named-pipe question waits for your decision (#3751). This is a `feat`, so it merges at the next cut, not now.

**What looks good**
- The CLI call reaches the same undoable command as the GUI and the MCP server. The call path is: `camcraft-cli --ui call` -> `link_client::call` (`crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:201`) -> a `tools/call` line (`link_client.rs:205`) -> the link `Inbox` (`crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs`) -> `mcp_host::pump` -> `answer_live_with(&state.world, &mut state.history, ...)` (`crates/ui/src/mcp_host.rs:60`) -> the MCP tool -> the command on the window's `History`. No document field is written directly.
- The live gate is the same as for `--mcp-port`: `LiveGate { approved: None, auto_approve_non_critical: false }`. So `post`, file writes, file-path arguments and machine or limit edits still need approval in the window.
- The new window test shows `add_operation` in the browser. Ctrl+Z removes it. So the call runs on the window's own history.
- No new dependency. The `--mcp-port` behaviour does not change. `port_from` moved to `crates/app/src/mcp/port_flag.rs` only to keep `listen.rs` under the 400-line law (`listen.rs` is 393 lines).
- The token gate is correct. The first line must carry the token from the discovery file. Any other first line is refused before a line reaches the app (`listen.rs:330-338`). On Unix the folder is 0700 and the socket and the file are 0600. The client never sends a token to an address that is not loopback (`link_client.rs:108-111`).
- The new code has no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic` outside tests. The discovery file and the socket are removed when the window's inbox drops (a test pins this).
- The exit codes are clear: no window 3, several windows 2, a refusal 1, a bad argument 2. The CLI never falls back to a headless document.
- The new tests are in the right place. `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs` joins the `mcp_live` directory suite, and its Gate map names `camcraft-app`. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/ui_link.rs` joins the `camcraft-ui` lib tests. No snapshot PNG changes. No post or toolpath change.

**Results (trial merge with `origin/main` `f2aa981b5`, built locally on Linux)**
The Unix socket arms (`#[cfg(unix)]`) compile and run here. The author built the Windows arms.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Trial merge with `origin/main` | clean, no conflicts |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_live` | 19 passed, 0 failed (the 5 new `--ui` link tests included) |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test cli` | 13 passed, 0 failed (`--ui` help lane walked) |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` | 304 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (cwd `crates/ui`) | 1586 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib ui_link` | 1 passed, 0 failed (the new window test) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | exit 0, no warnings |
| `cargo xtask gate light` | green: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (wall 5.9 min; 11 light twins) |

The gate maps the changed `app::mcp` hub module to all app suites (186 steps). I ran the touched binaries by name (AGENTS.md "Test the change"). The author reports the full quick gate green on this head (185 steps, 0 failed).

**Targeted tests**
- Example catalog: no post or toolpath change, so none ran.
- Light lane: `cargo xtask gate light` -> green. Steps: build 6 s, motion lib 282 s, `adaptive_troch_island` 34 s, `adaptive_troch_neck` 13 s, `adaptive_troch_parallel` 9 s, app `pocket_pass_start` 11 s. 0 failed, 0 stalled. The first attempt hit my 10-minute command limit on the release build (578 s). The re-run, with the build cached, is the result above.
- Heavy: this is a `P2` PR, so it gets no heavy step (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review").

**Requested before merge**
- None.

**Questions and notes (not blocking)**
1. There is no response timeout after the hello. `link_client::call` sets the read timeout to `None` after the 5 s hello (`link_client.rs:133-135`), because a tool such as `generate` can take minutes. If the window's UI thread stops, the CLI waits with no limit. This matches `--mcp-port`. A keepalive or a longer bound can be a later change.
2. The listener serves one client at a time. While a long `--ui call` runs, a second CLI's hello read times out after 5 s, and it says "the link files ... are stale" with exit 3 (`link_client.rs:181-184`), although a window is running. The decision file accepts one client at a time. A distinct message, "the window is busy", is a possible follow-up.
3. `--ui mcp` over an idle window: the server drops an idle client after 5 minutes (`IDLE_TIMEOUT`), so the bridge exits with 0. This matches `--mcp-port`.
4. `--ui mcp` (`link_client::bridge`) has no test of its own. It reuses the tested `connect`. The author states this in the body.
5. The `camcraft-mcp` skill's "Live GUI session" row names only `--mcp-port`. A line for `--ui` would help an agent. No new MCP tool is added, so no skill row is required by the law.

<!-- review-cost: effort medium, no escalation -->

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
